title: Design System: Leonardo Carvalho, fifth edition

glass-night.note: Shader tint vec3(.15,.20,.90) mixed at 48% into windows and ornaments at night. Light in a surface, never a CSS fill.

glass-prominent.note: The prominent glass kind: vec3(.16,.34,1.0) at 46%, brightened 16%; by day vec3(.24,.46,1.0) (#3d75ff). Exempt from the brightness cap. It was the hello's Enter button; since the hero made the title the control no element carries it.

glass-day.note: Shader tint vec3(.10,.16,.40) by day, under the 0.22 luminance cap.

room-night-horizon.note: The violet horizon; the night deep base is #040a47.

room-day-horizon.note: The warm pale day horizon; the day deep base is #082994.

ground-night.note: html background under room-night.webp, theme colour, text on white controls.

paper.note: The manuscript card and figure grounds.

card-ink.note: Text on Paper, Gold and Sand cards; written as a literal (#1b1b1f) in four rules.

drawn-ink.note: A drawn Work card; literal in CSS.

drawn-violet.note: A drawn Work card; literal in CSS.

drawn-green.note: A drawn Work card; literal in CSS.

ink.note: All primary text. Defined as --ink but used through the token only twice; #fff is written as a literal about 36 times.

line.note: Dividers inside list groups and tables. Same value as Fill 2.

fill-2.note: Hover and icon wells. The toolbar writes .15 as a literal instead.

fill-3.note: The tab bubble and hovered close button.

tint.note: CSS glass at night, under blur(30px) saturate(1.7) brightness(.8).

title.purpose: Window and sheet titles on every page but home; 30px under 900px.

headline.purpose: Section titles inside a window; inline side-window titles.

lede.purpose: Introduction and contact sentence; first sentence bold in Ink. 17px under 900px.

lead.purpose: The first-person sentence heading each record group.

control.purpose: Buttons, links as controls; tabs at 16px.

meta.purpose: Dates, sublines, side-window text, references, captions.

caption.purpose: Card sublines, table heads, experiment dates. Nothing under 12px.

manuscript.purpose: The aducanumab manuscript's own title, on its sheet and (15px) on its card. The only serif.

name-hero.purpose: Switzer 780, min(8.2vw, 24svh, 160px), -.03em: one line from 700px wide, two lines below at min(18vw, 15svh, 120px). Solid glass drawn by the room; CSS glass without it.

name-title.purpose: Switzer 700, 46px (42px under 900px, 44px on two lines under 700px, 30px on short landscape phones), -.03em, white text: the glyphs the hero lands on.

hint.purpose: 500 14px Ink 2, centred 32px above the foot of the screen: "Click the title to proceed" ("Tap" on coarse pointers).

shadows.name: window-drawn
shadows.value: room shader: offset 22px down, reach 90px, strength .34
shadows.purpose: Every window and sheet, cast into the room.

shadows.name: ornament-drawn
shadows.value: room shader: offset 22px down, reach 40px, strength .22

shadows.name: phone-tab-bar
shadows.purpose: The phone bottom tab bar, always CSS glass.

shadows.name: screenshot
shadows.value: 0 10px 26px rgba(0, 0, 0, .26) on cards; 0 14px 34px rgba(0, 0, 0, .24) on figures
shadows.purpose: A screenshot resting on its colour.

shadows.name: hover-light
shadows.value: radial-gradient(180px circle at var(--hx) var(--hy), rgba(255,255,255,.16), transparent 62%), plus-lighter; pressed 240px at .30
shadows.purpose: The visionOS gaze light on [data-hover] elements.

shadows.name: focus
shadows.purpose: Every focusable element; the hero's name takes the same ring 12px out, rounded at .2em.

shadows.name: tab-bubble
shadows.purpose: The top edge of the current-tab bubble.

shadows.name: hero-light
shadows.value: Gaussian blur of the letters, 30% of the font size; added to the room at .5 by night, .26 by day; a tighter leak at the edges (mip 3 of the letters); leans up to 5% of the font size toward the pointer; hover x1.22, a press flares it
shadows.purpose: The light behind the hero's name, in the color style's hue.

glass.name: frost
glass.value: mip level log2(max(4, 26 * dpr)); controls one level less
glass.purpose: Blur read from the room texture.

glass.name: lensing
glass.value: edge band 30px (windows) or 20px (others); bend = edge^2 * 26px (windows) or 16px
glass.purpose: The room bends inward near the rounded edge.

glass.name: tint
glass.value: night vec3(.15,.20,.90), day vec3(.10,.16,.40), mixed 48% (windows, ornaments), 22% (controls), prominent 46% of vec3(.16,.34,1.0)/(.24,.46,1.0) and x1.16

glass.name: brightness-cap
glass.value: non-prominent glass scaled so luminance <= 0.22 before rim and light are added

glass.name: rim
glass.value: gaussian 1.1px at the edge, 0.8 * (0.30 + 0.55 * facing the light); edge glow 0.06 * edge^2
glass.purpose: The bright edge of Liquid Glass.

glass.name: pointer-highlight
glass.value: gaussian sigma 300px around the light position, +0.06
glass.purpose: A pool of light that follows the pointer (spring .6 / 1).

glass.name: press-light
glass.value: 0.24 * press of vec3(.92,.96,1.0), sigma 7% of viewport height, at the pointer
glass.purpose: A pressed control lights from within.

glass.name: hero-ink
glass.value: mask canvas (letters, a height blurred 3.5% of the font size, the light behind blurred 30%) turned to solid glass: frosted faces (the room at the frost level x1.12, lit from behind), a rim 0.95 facing the light and 0.38 behind, the far bevel shaded 38%, a highlight drawn toward the pointer, a faint moving surface and a sheen every 9s; by day the faces a deeper cobalt; mixed fully to white as it becomes the title
glass.purpose: The hero's name, until it hands off to the HTML title.

motion.name: spring-model
motion.value: response (s) and damping ratio; 4ms substeps; settles within 1e-3

motion.name: motion-rules
motion.value: no blur on text in motion; nothing moves on its own; 150 to 300ms and at most about 8px of travel for UI; critically damped for anything with text; staggers of 40 to 80ms

motion.name: window-materialise
motion.value: response .5, damping 1; from scale(.985) (8px at most at the corners); opacity at 1.4x the spring

motion.name: side-materialise
motion.value: response .55, damping 1; from 32deg to 24deg, with the fade
motion.purpose: The side window arriving (it stays in place across page changes).

motion.name: tab-bubble
motion.value: response .45, damping .8; stretch up to 30% along travel at |v|/3000

motion.name: sheet-back
motion.value: response .5, damping 1; parent translateZ(-4vw), contents brightness .5, saturate .8 (no blur), the window's contents gone by 25% of the travel (its toolbar and window bar by 40%)
motion.purpose: A sheet opening over its parent.

motion.name: room-lean
motion.value: response .9, damping 1; room shift x*.012, -y*.008; the windows never move with the pointer
motion.purpose: Desktop only, not under reduced motion.

motion.name: pointer-light
motion.purpose: The glass light following the pointer.

motion.name: window-bar-drag
motion.value: rubber d*40/(40+|d|); home on response .5, damping .7

motion.name: hero-arrival
motion.value: glass and light up on response .8, damping 1 (about 0.9s); the hint from .75s over .5s

motion.name: hero-enter
motion.value: hint out 120ms; focus pull response 1 damping 1; the glide response .65 damping 1 (about 0.7s), size in log space, weight 780 to 700, to white; the window's glass at once; its contents (240ms) once the name is within .6 of the title's size of its slot, then side window +60ms, tab bar +120ms, toolbar and window bar +180ms; hand-off: the HTML title fades in 150ms over the ink, then the ink out 100ms

motion.name: page-swap
motion.value: out 140ms cubic-bezier(.4,0,1,1): opacity only; in 220ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1): opacity from 6px down; no blur, no scale; the side window's contents crossfade with the window's

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: CSS micro-motion: tab bar width .42s, labels .3s, button press .35s, card hover .45s, the hero's hint .5s.

motion.name: room-drift
motion.value: crest undulation and form drift over tens of seconds; 60fps while anything moves, 30fps while only the room drifts

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: no glide, focus pull, lean, drift or springs; the hero shown at once; transitions .15s; no animations; room still

drift: --ink is defined but used through the token twice; #fff is written as a literal about 36 times (text, focus, button fills).
The glass kind 'control' is defined in panels.js and handled by the shader (22% tint, one frost level less) but no element carries data-glass="control"; only window, ornament and prominent are used.
#0b1138 (Night Ground, text on white controls) and #1b1b1f (Card Ink) are repeated as literals, not tokens; the three drawn card colours are literals too.
--r-win (32px) is used once; the tab bar writes 32px, side windows 28px, side rows 16px (= --r-row), the portrait 20px (= --r-card) and toc links 12px as literals.
:focus-visible sets border-radius 10px globally, which changes the corner of any element without its own radius while focused.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "One Room, Many Windows"**

A cobalt room drawn the way Apple draws its Liquid Glass wallpapers: a navy sky falling to a violet horizon, soft out-of-focus cobalt and periwinkle forms, and a flat glass wave with one bright crest, all moving slowly. The room is one WebGL2 canvas behind everything, in two palettes that follow the system: Night (navy and violet) and Day (sky blue over a warm pale horizon). Into that room the site floats glass windows as visionOS does: one main window, a tab bar just off its left edge, a toolbar crossing its bottom edge, a small window bar under it that drags and springs home, and at 1360px and wider one side window turned 24 degrees toward the reader; tab bar, main window and side window are set as one group, centred on the screen. Projects open as sheets in front of the window you came from, which steps back a little and dims.

The front door is the hero. On the first home view of a session the room is out of focus and "Leonardo Carvalho" stands in the middle of it in Switzer at 780, heavy and blocky, drawn by the room as solid glass: frosted faces, bright rims, and a light behind the letters that spills round them in the colour style's hue. The specular light and that glow lean gently toward the pointer, hovering lifts the light and a press flares it. At the foot of the screen one quiet line says "Click the title to proceed" ("Tap" on touch screens). The title is the control: clicking it (or Return) pulls the room into focus while the name glides into the main window's title slot, turning white, and the window's glass forms around it; the window's contents, the side window and the tab bar follow, and the name hands off to the HTML title, which is plain text from then on. Liquid Glass stays out of the content layer, as Apple asks. Everything else is the system UI face, set the way visionOS sets it.

The material is glass drawn by the room itself: frost read from the blurred room, lensing at the rounded edge, a cobalt tint, a brightness cap that keeps white text legible, a bright rim, a light that follows the pointer, and a light from within when a control is pressed. Inside a window nothing is glass again: lists, cards, tables and buttons are white fills at 6, 14 and 22 percent. Motion is springs everywhere, described as Apple describes them (a response and a damping ratio) and stepped in the same frame as the glass. Nothing that carries text blurs or moves on its own: page changes crossfade, windows stay where they are when the pointer moves (only the light follows it, and the room behind leans), and anything with text settles without overshoot.
keyCharacteristics: A drawn cobalt room (Night and Day) behind every page; a still of each is the CSS background without WebGL or scripts.
Glass windows and ornaments, and the hero's name, drawn by the room under the HTML; CSS glass as the fallback.
The name in Switzer is the only display voice: solid glass in the hero, white text as the home title; the system face sets everything else in white at three levels.
Concentric radii: phone sheet 40, window 32, side window 28, card 20, list group 16, pill for every control.
One spring model (response, damping) for materialising, the hero's glide, the tab bubble, sheets, drag and press; no blur on text in motion.
Every page reads without JavaScript, calms under reduced motion and transparency, and prints on white Letter.

rules.name: The White on Glass Rule
rules.body: Text is white at 100, 78 or 71 percent and nothing else, on glass that caps its own brightness (relative luminance at most 0.22 before the rim and highlights are added), so every level keeps 4.5:1 over the night glass and the bright day room alike.

rules.name: The Room Is the Colour Rule
rules.body: The site's own saturated colour lives in the room and in the glass tint drawn from it. The only other colour is a project's own, on its card and its figures.

rules.name: The Fills Not Glass Rule
rules.body: Inside a window, surfaces are white fills (6, 14, 22 percent), never a second layer of glass or a coloured panel.

rules.name: The Name Rule
rules.body: The only display type is the name in Switzer: solid glass in the hero, white text as the home title. Headings never borrow it, and the system face never goes above the 34px title.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Everything that is read is the system UI face, the name apart. The serif appears only as the manuscript's own title, on its card and its sheet; the experiments' titles lean in italic at 550 in the same face.

rules.name: The Bold Is Ink Rule
rules.body: Inside Ink 2 text, a bold phrase is lifted to white at 650. Weight and ink rise together.

rules.name: The One Glass Layer Rule
rules.body: Glass is for windows and the controls that float over them. Nothing inside a window is glass: buttons, lists and cards are fills.

rules.name: The Legibility Cap Rule
rules.body: The glass holds its own brightness down before light is added to its edges, so white text reads whatever the room is doing behind it.

dos: Do let the name be the display voice: Switzer in solid glass in the hero, white text as the home title, with scripts off and in print (The Name Rule).
Do keep text white at 100, 78 or 71 percent on glass, and let the glass cap its own brightness (The White on Glass Rule).
Do put surfaces inside a window on the three fills (6, 14, 22 percent) and keep glass for windows and the controls that float over them (The One Glass Layer Rule).
Do keep corners concentric: 40, 32, 28, 20, 16, 12 and the capsule for controls.
Do move geometry with springs given as response and damping, in the same frame as the glass, and give reduced motion 150ms crossfades.
Do give a project card its own screen's colour, with its screenshot resting on it.
Do turn the side window toward the reader as a resting position, keep it in place across page changes, and turn it in from a little further round (32 degrees) when it first arrives.
Do keep every page readable with scripts off, under reduced transparency (CSS glass at 84% tint), in forced colours, and in print.
donts: Don't put glass inside glass: no frosted panel, card or button inside a window.
Don't tint text or headings; colour belongs to the room, the glass and a project's card.
Don't set a heading in a script or a display face, or set the system face larger than the 34px title.
Don't tilt anything in response to hover; the side window's angle is its place in the room, and hover answers with light and scale.
Don't blur text or a window's contents while they move, and don't move windows with the pointer: blur and lean belong to the room behind.
Don't fade a sheet's parent through its glass without fading its contents; the room cannot frost HTML.
Don't put a small label above a title or section heading; the title carries itself.
Don't use tween durations for window, bubble or sheet motion; those are springs.
